name: Rich Black (FOGRA29)
lede: Rich Black (FOGRA29) names a print-industry black mixed from more than one ink, calibrated to FOGRA's uncoated-paper standard.

sections.title: From a printing term to a swatch
sections.body:
"Rich black" is a printing term for an ink mixture of solid black over one or more of the other CMYK inks, giving a darker result than black ink alone [1]. FOGRA, a German printing-research body, publishes registered characterization data sets that describe how ink behaves on specific papers under ISO offset-printing conditions; FOGRA29 (also called OFCOM 4, Altona) describes uncoated white paper at 120 grams per square meter [2]. This swatch is a flat screen approximation of that printing condition, not a measured ink sample [1][2].

Its closest sibling in the library is [[rich-black-fogra39]], the equivalent standard for coated paper, and both sit near plain [[black]] on screen [1].

It also sits close to the generic near-blacks [[near-black]] and [[rich-black-fogra39]], both read as almost the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this near-black hue appears in 1,202 of 23,781 paintings, about 5.1 percent, as photographed [3]. It is most common around the 1690s, and Pieter van der Werff and Arnoud van Halen use it far more than the archive average relative to their output [3]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, and a near-black match says little about the actual ink or pigment used [3].
